about: Reader-setting spans and verse markers, implemented twice: owb/markup.py (validation, the build) and web/markup.js (the reader). Settings change wording, never meaning, so both must give the same text. tests/test_markup.py and tests/js/markup.test.mjs run every case. 'cases': text + settings -> rendered text, and (where given) that text split at its verse markers as [verse or null, text]. 'differences': inputs where the two implementations currently disagree, with each one's answer, so a change on either side is noticed.

cases.name: plain text is unchanged
cases.text: In the beginning was the Word.
cases.rendered: In the beginning was the Word.
verses: In the beginning was the Word.

cases.name: units default
cases.text: about {{units:20 to 30 gallons|two or three measures}}

cases.name: units alternate
cases.text: about {{units:20 to 30 gallons|two or three measures}}

cases.name: several settings at once
cases.text: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to {{gender:all people|men}}; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, about {{christos:the Messiah|Christ}}
cases.rendered: Yahweh spoke to all people; His word, about Christ

cases.name: one setting leaves the others at their defaults
span at the start and end
index out of range shows the default
a string index shows the default
a null index shows the default
an unknown setting with no value shows its default
names with digits are not spans
an unclosed span is left alone
braces inside a span stop it matching the outer braces
one verse marker
cases.text: children of God \v 13 children born of God.
cases.rendered: children of God \v 13 children born of God.

cases.name: a span on each side of a marker
a backslash-v without a number is not a marker
a marker straight after the last verse, no space before it

differences.name: a value for a setting the reader does not offer
differences.note: Python only honours names in SETTINGS; JS reads any name from the settings object. The reader's object also holds view, headings, uncertain and level, so a span named one of those would follow that control. No content uses such a name (owb.validate rejects it).

differences.name: a boolean index
differences.note: Python's bool is an int, so True picks option 1; JS takes only numbers. The reader stores numbers, so this does not arise in practice.

differences.name: whitespace before a later marker
differences.note: Python right-strips every part before a marker; JS trims only the first part. Every sentence that crosses two verse boundaries hits this (1,453 in content/ when this was written); the reader puts the trailing space into the verse's text, where HTML collapses it.

differences.name: leading whitespace in the first part
differences.note: JS trims both ends of the first part, Python only the end. No content text with verse markers starts with a space today.
